q: Running more trials fixes a wrong model.
why: Myth. More runs shrink only the noise; model bias stays the same however many runs you do.

q: Plugging average inputs into a model gives the average output.
why: Myth. For a nonlinear model, f(average input) differs from the average of f: the flaw of averages.

q: Which inequality says a convex model's average output is at least its output at the average input?
why: Jensen's inequality gives the direction of the flaw of averages.

q: Stock 100 at cost 4, sell at 10, demand uniform on 50 to 150. Profit at average demand (100)?
Same shop: what is the true expected profit? (E[min(100, D)] = 87.5)
why: 10 × 87.5 − 400 = 475, far below the 600 at average demand.

q: Two normal costs with SD 20 are positively correlated. Compared with independence, the mean of the total is …
why: Correlation does not change the mean of a sum, only its spread and tails.

q: A normal distribution is a safe default for financial losses.
why: Myth. Losses have fat tails; a t with 3 degrees of freedom puts about 100× more probability beyond 4 SDs.

q: P(loss) = 0.23 from 1,000 runs. What is the MCSE? (decimal)
An MCMC chain has lag-1 autocorrelation 0.9. Effective sample size is about N divided by …
Daily returns use the annual volatility 0.20 as the daily SD. The simulated yearly SD is about …
why: Variance adds over 252 days: 0.20 × √252 ≈ 3.2; the daily SD should be 0.20/√252.
